$comment: WHAT THE HARDCODING AUDIT LOOKS AT. Declared here so narrowing or widening the scan is a config edit that shows up in review, rather than an edit inside the scanner that quietly changes what every count means.
$why: The audit swept orchestrations/config and orchestrations/agents JSON, on the argument that a shipped default is an engine fact. That made the headline number unreadable: 205 of 658 sites were llm-defaults.*.json naming the models it exists to name, and profiles.json holding the personas it exists to hold. Those files ARE the configuration the engine reads — the opposite of a value baked into code. Operator decision 2026-08-26: json and config are not hardcoding.
$careful: Narrowing a scanner is how a scanner comes to report clean while the defect it was written for is still there. The scope may only be narrowed to exclude DECLARATION files — never code. A test asserts the scanner still finds engine sites.
$excludeWhy: Tests are excluded because a fixture naming a client is not a shipped fact. Per-project launchers are excluded because a launcher exists to declare ONE project's facts — configuration living in the file that owns it. Vendored trees are not ours. "/test/" excludes a test DIRECTORY, which the .test./.spec. infixes did not: orchestrations/scripts/test/test-epam-providers.sh contributed 6 model-identifier findings for models it exists to exercise, while the header already declared tests out of scope. Anchored on the directory, so engine files merely NAMED test-something (test-engine.sh) are still scanned.
